Title: Pareto frontier lines for AI are great but where are the Pareto planes?
HN text: Pareto frontier lines are used a lot for comparing tradeoffs between two different attributes in AI models.
I want to be able to see the Pareto frontier planes for 3 attributes (which probably look closer to a bumpy dome, similar to how pareto lines are actually more like bumpy curves).
And although you wouldn't be able to visualize a pareto cube/tesseract for 4+ attributes, it might still be useful in some way.

A few months ago I wrote about “good enough” models , arguing that cheap models had gotten smart enough for most coding work, and that the expensive frontier models were best saved for the tasks that actually need them. That’s mostly played out as expected. Which leaves a new question: once you’re sure you don’t need the smartest model for a task, how do you find the cheapest one that’s still smart enough?
